notes.title: Bowing hello
notes.text: Koreans greet with a small bow and 안녕하세요 (literally "Are you at peace?"). Bow a little lower for older people. 처음 뵙겠습니다 is the formal "nice to meet you" for a first meeting; 반가워요 is the everyday version.

notes.title: This, that and that over there
notes.text: Korean has three "this/that" words: 이 (near me), 그 (near you, or something just mentioned) and 저 (over there, away from both of us). Add 거 for "thing": 이거, 그거, 저거.

notes.title: Floors
notes.text: In Korea, the ground floor is 1층 (first floor), like in the US. Basements are 지하 (underground): 지하 1층 = B1.

notes.title: Calling people by name
notes.text: Koreans add 씨 after a full name or given name (민준 씨) to be polite with peers. Never use 씨 with your own name, and don't use it for older people like Grandma or a teacher; use a title like 할머니 or 선생님 instead.

notes.title: Two goodbyes
notes.text: The person leaving says 안녕히 계세요 ("stay in peace"). The person staying says 안녕히 가세요 ("go in peace"). With friends and kids, just 안녕!
